kata.name: Abstract-factory near-floor control - a two-kind, two-factory grid where the frozen four-cell factory sample catches every injected fault
kata.series_report: docs/ref/pattern-kata-dispositions.md row Abstract Factory (`disposed — construction only; no invariant on a finite instance`); fixtures/katas/abstract-factory/README.md (pre-registered); beads catherine-r5k.1
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: at the two-kind/two-factory floor the conventional four-cell sample catches both seeded faults; the probe buys zero unique detections (killed)

expected.detail: declared site (ModernFactory, chair) has cell_product = null; the frozen sample includes that cell, so the conventional arm catches the executed dangling finding
declared site (VictorianFactory, sofa) realizes a modern sofa; the frozen sample includes that cell, so the conventional arm catches the executed T4 family-coherence violation

commands: python3 prototype/abstract_factory_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: control faults 2/2 caught; 3 unique elements suite-wide
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/abstract-factory/near-floor.ct.json --json  # exit 0, findings []
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/abstract-factory/near-floor-fault-missing.ct.json --json  # exit 4, 1 dangling
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/abstract-factory/near-floor-fault-family.ct.json --json  # exit 3, 1 violation

comparison.conventional_baseline: prototype/abstract_factory_baseline.py: a frozen four-pair sample (both factories x chair, sofa) of factory-call assertions plus both kinds; catches both injected faults (2/2), zero unique detections for the probe.

baseline.artifact: prototype/abstract_factory_baseline.py sha256:4f635702ad371a9c1155965763f18e2fda0d8a6289455fb708fe60e2dcb07c97 (frozen per-fixture (factory, kind) sample; always executed before the probe arm)

expressibility_gap.invariant: control scope: every injected fault lies inside the pre-registered four-cell sample
expressibility_gap.why: the near-floor control measures what a complete two-by-two sample catches; it says nothing about sites outside the sample, which is the scoped claim of the positive entries

discrepancies: Control scope: both seeded faults are cell-local and the sample is complete at this floor; the control is a parity demonstration, not a claim that the conventional arm is exhaustive above the floor.
procedure: 1. The law (AF-T, declared-grid product-family totality) and the fault matrix were committed in fixtures/katas/abstract-factory/ before any recorded run (README.md, faults.json); the pre-registration sections are not edited after the run.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/abstract_factory_baseline.py, sha256 pinned in comparison.baseline.artifact) was executed first: a frozen per-fixture sample of (factory, kind) realization sites asserting exactly one declared Cell, a resolved product, kind agreement, family agreement, plus one coverage assertion per sampled kind. Sites outside the sample are never inspected.

3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real CLI: `catherine check --json`. Witnesses were mapped to presentation elements cell:<Factory>/<Kind> (dangling on cell_product/cell_factory/cell_kind, equation violations on a Cell row, key collisions on the shared site) and kind:<Kind> (dangling on kind_witness).

4. unique_detections = executed probe elements minus baseline-identified elements. The constructed catalog is not consulted (the kata id is unregistered there, so expectations are the pre-registered rows in this record). A construction rejection is recorded but never counted.

5. Verdict follows the recorded rule: empty unique = killed; non-empty unique with an executed baseline arm = survived; a claim resting only on a hypothesis or construction probe would be inconclusive.
